speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a postpartum patient with fever and abdominal tenderness; can you tell me exactly when your delivery occurred and whether it was vaginal or a C-section?

Also, have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge, chills, or difficulty urinating?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details; the "11-pound" baby suggests macrosomia, which can complicate the delivery. Since you mentioned decreased bowel sounds and uterine tenderness, I need to know if you have any shoulder pain or if you've had any episodes of vomiting. Also, have you noticed any swelling or redness around your incision or perineum?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, and Blood_Culture
REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Pelvic_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC, CRP, Blood_Culture: Pending; Urinalysis: Pending; Abdominal_Pelvic_X-Ray: Pending

speaker: Doctor
text: While we wait for your lab and X-ray results, can you tell me if you have experienced any rectal pain or a sensation of fullness/pressure in the rectum, and are you able to pass gas? Additionally, has your abdominal pain become significantly worse since delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Pelvic Infection with possible Uterine Atony.

Given the fever, uterine tenderness, and decreased bowel sounds after a prolonged labor with macrosomia, this likely represents a severe endometritis or a pelvic abscess rather than a simple urinary tract infection. I recommend an urgent pelvic ultrasound to evaluate for retained products of conception or an abscess before we proceed with antibiotics.
